Body: Tried just now, did not help:

We hit the same class of failures with OpenAI-compatible custom providers. In our case, the provider would often answer once with text or legacy tool payloads and then the OpenCode session stopped instead of continuing into a real tool loop.

We got this working in a fork with an opt-in compatibility layer instead of treating every custom provider like native OpenAI:

- provider-level tool parser middleware
- normalization for legacy `message.function_call` and streamed `delta.function_call`
- parsing for text-only tool intents, JSON tool blocks, and wrapped `<tool_call>` payloads
- optional session repair when a tool-capable turn ends with `finish_reason=stop` but no usable tool call was recognized
- provider request adapter for endpoints that accept `functions/function_call` more reliably than `tools/tool_choice`
- tool allowlist / minimized tool payload for brittle custom providers

Live result on our side: a previously broken OpenAI-compatible endpoint that answered once and stopped was able to continue multi-turn tool execution in OpenCode.

This likely overlaps with the blank/empty custom-provider reports in #15756, #5210, and #10573.

If useful, I can package this into a PR as an explicit custom-provider compatibility path so the default behavior for native providers stays unchanged.

We ran into a very similar custom-provider failure mode. In our case the direct API worked, but OpenCode either returned effectively blank output or stopped after the first step because the provider only partially matched the OpenAI tool / stream schema.

What fixed it in our fork was an opt-in compatibility layer for custom OpenAI-compatible providers:

- request adapter for `tools` / `tool_choice` -> legacy `functions` / `function_call` when needed
- parser middleware for legacy `function_call`, text-only tool intents, JSON tool blocks, and wrapped `<tool_call>` payloads
- optional session repair when a custom provider ends a tool-capable turn with `finish_reason=stop`
- minimized tool payload / allowlist for brittle providers

That was enough to turn a previously blank / one-shot OpenAI-compatible endpoint into a usable multi-turn tool flow on our side.

This seems related to the same family of issues discussed in #234, #5210, and #10573.

If maintainers want, I can turn the compatibility layer into a PR behind explicit custom-provider config so it does not affect the happy path for native providers.

Greptile Summary

This PR systematically replaces all remaining `bun` shell (`$\`...\``) invocations across the opencode CLI and core with the shared `Process.run`/`Process.text`/`git()` helpers, eliminating the runtime dependency on Bun's shell API for command execution. The refactor spans 16 files covering git operations, LSP server installs, clipboard, ripgrep, snapshots, archive extraction, and the upgrade/uninstall flows. Key changes: - **`util/process.ts`**: Adds `TextResult`, `text()`, and `lines()` helpers plus a `.catch` handler that converts spawn-level errors to a `code: 1` result when `nothrow: true`, providing a uniform API surface. - **`cli/cmd/github.ts`**: Extracts `gitText`, `gitRun`, `gitStatus`, and `commitChanges` closures; updates error handling to catch `Process.RunFailedError` instead of `$.ShellError`; migrates all git operations to the shared `git()` helper. - **`installation/index.ts`**: Replaces `curl | bash` with a `fetch`-then-`Process.spawn` pattern for the curl upgrade path; breaks the brew tap upgrade chain into individually-checked steps — though an empty path returned by `brew --repo` will silently skip `git pull --ff-only` rather than surfacing an error. - **`lsp/server.ts`**: Replaces `chmod +x` with `fs.chmod`, `curl` downloads with `fetch`/`Filesystem.writeStream`, and `ls glob` with `fs.readdir` + regex; local `run`/`output` helpers unconditionally force `nothrow: true`. - **`snapshot/index.ts`**: Splits the `read-tree && checkout-index` shell pipeline into two sequential `Process.run` calls with per-step error logging. - **`file/ripgrep.ts`**: Correctly removes shell quoting around the `--glob=!.git/*` argument (quotes were shell artefacts stripped by the old shell interpreter; passing directly to the process argv requires the unquoted form).

Confidence Score: 4/5

- PR is safe to merge with one logic edge case to verify in the brew upgrade path. - The refactor is mechanically consistent across all 16 files and preserves prior semantics in the vast majority of cases. The `git()` helper's `nothrow: true` design matches the original `.nothrow()` usage throughout. The one logic concern is in `installation/index.ts` where a successfully-exiting `brew --repo` that returns an empty string silently skips the `git pull --ff-only` step and proceeds to upgrade; the old shell pipeline would have failed. All other changes are equivalent or strictly improved (better error messages, no shell injection via template strings, `fs.realpath`/`fs.chmod` replacing shell commands). - packages/opencode/src/installation/index.ts (brew upgrade tap path)

This PR removes the `"search returns match metadata"` test from `packages/opencode/test/file/ripgrep.test.ts`, leaving `Ripgrep.search` covered only by a no-match negative case. - **Coverage gap introduced**: The deleted test was the sole test exercising `Ripgrep.search` with a real match. The function's pipeline — shell command construction, `JSON.parse`, Zod schema validation, `.filter(r => r.type === "match")`, and `.map(r => r.data)` — is now untested for the positive path. - **No indirect coverage**: `GrepTool` (tested in `test/tool/grep.test.ts`) calls `Ripgrep.filepath()` directly and does its own parsing; it does **not** call `Ripgrep.search`, so the gap is real. - **Misleading framing**: The PR description labels the removed test as "unused coverage," but the test was actively exercising the core match-returning behavior of `search()`, not a redundant or dead code path.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Safe to merge if the author intentionally accepts reduced coverage for `Ripgrep.search`, but the positive-match path is now completely untested. - The change itself is low-risk (deleting a test cannot break production code), but it removes the only test validating that `Ripgrep.search` correctly returns match metadata, leaving a meaningful coverage gap in a non-trivial parsing pipeline. - packages/opencode/test/file/ripgrep.test.ts — only file changed; the deletion of the positive-path test deserves review.

Tested this fix locally. Works as expected in new sessions — /undo then /redo correctly preserves file timestamps on untouched files.

One edge case worth noting: if /undo was performed on older code (before this fix), the revert record stored in the session won't have the files field. When /redo runs with the new code, it hits the backward-compat fallback and does the old blanket checkout-index -a -f, reproducing the original bug. This is by design — the fix requires both /undo and /redo to run on the new code. Once the old revert is cleared (by redoing and undoing again with the new code), subsequent /redo operations work correctly.

Not a bug — just a one-time edge case for sessions with pre-fix revert state.
